question: The following statements regarding insulin resistance in diabetic patients are true except:

options.opa: It is more common with huminsulin
options.opb: It may occur in the presence of infections
options.opc: It may be due to antibodies to insulin
options.opd: Use of glucocorticoids may be useful in severe cases

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Insulin resistance" -> "often associated with type 2 diabetes" -> "more common with human insulin" -> "true statement" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Insulin resistance" -> "can occur during infections" -> "true statement" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Insulin resistance" -> "may be due to antibodies to insulin" -> "possible but not common" -> "unclear" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Insulin resistance" -> "use of glucocorticoids" -> "may worsen insulin resistance" -> "not useful in severe cases" -> 85%
analysis: Insulin resistance is a common feature in diabetic patients, particularly in type 2 diabetes. The statements provided can be evaluated as follows: 1) The statement that insulin resistance is more common with human insulin (opa) is true, as human insulin can lead to a higher incidence of insulin resistance compared to other forms of insulin. 2) The statement that insulin resistance may occur in the presence of infections (opb) is also true, as infections can induce a state of insulin resistance due to inflammatory cytokines. 3) The statement that insulin resistance may be due to antibodies to insulin (opc) is less common and not a primary cause of insulin resistance, but it is possible in certain cases. 4) The statement regarding the use of glucocorticoids (opd) is false; glucocorticoids are known to exacerbate insulin resistance rather than provide a therapeutic benefit in severe cases. Therefore, the statement that is not true is the one regarding glucocorticoids. This aligns with the consensus in pharmacology and endocrinology that glucocorticoids worsen insulin resistance. Thus, the best-supported option is opd.
